newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva to auction film star, royal and jetset gems.
newsitem.headline: Geneva to auction film star, royal and jetset gems.

text.p: A Bulgari gold necklace worn by Sharon Stone in the film "Casino" and other dazzling designer jewels from the gem box of a jet-set Lebanese divorcee are among treasures up for auction in Geneva next week.

New owners are also sought for historic valuables - a pink diamond believed to have belonged to France's Queen Marie-Antoinette, emeralds said to come from Russian Empress Catherine the Great and an emerald and diamond brooch owned by Italy's Queen Margherita.
Buyers from the Far East, New York and Europe are expected to flock to luxury hotels along Lake Geneva, where the autumn sales by Christie's and Sotheby's are held.
"There is an enormous amount of jewellery on sale in Geneva next week. It will be a bit of a test for the market," David Bennett, head of Sotheby's jewellery department, told Reuters.

Antiquorum Auctioneers and the Parisian auction house Etude Tajan are teaming up to sell 600 pieces by Cartier, billed as a "world premiere". Cartier says it will issue authenticity certificates as part of a "fight against forgeries".
But Tuesday's sale of the personal collection of Mouna al-Ayoub, the glamorous Lebanese former wife of Saudi businessman Nasser Al-Rachid, is expected to hold the spotlight.

The mother of five is parting with 146 lots expected to bring in between $8 million-$10 million on Tuesday evening, according to Christie's. Press reports say the 39-year-old needs the money to set up a charity foundation in Majorca.

A Bulgari three-row beaded necklace, matching bracelet and pair of earrings -- worn by the steamy Stone in Martin Scorsese's film "Casino" last year -- is among the pieces being sold off by the divorcee.
"The suite was worn by Sharon Stone in the film and bought later by Mouna Al-Ayoub," a Christie's spokeswoman told Reuters.
Stone was nominated for an Oscar for her role as Ginger McKenna, the high-price call girl who marries a Las Vegas casino operator and then degenerates into a pill-popping alcoholic.

Al-Ayoub, now Paris-based and an avid collector of French designer clothes, is due to attend the weekend viewing of her opulent collection, which includes contemporary pieces by Bulgari, Cartier and Van Cleef & Arpels and Harry Winston.

Francois Curiel, director of Christie's international jewellery department, will conduct the sale. A year ago he landed $27 million for the jewels of Princess Salimah Aga Khan, a British-born former model and divorced wife of the Aga Khan.

The auction -- boosted by a lawsuit brought by her husband, the spirital leader of the Ismaili Moslem community, who contested the Begum's right to sell off all of the family jewels -- nearly doubled its pre-sale estimate.
"There is no lawsuit connected with this sale," a Christie's spokeswoman said of the al-Ayoub collection.
The star lot of the al-Ayoub collection is a stunning ring by Geneva jeweller Harry Winston, with a rectangular diamond of 31.19 carats. It is estimated to bring in a cool $one million.

On Thursday, Christie's will auction a diamond brooch with a 47.76 carat Colombian emerald in the centre, given to Margherita of Savoy-Genoa in 1868 for her marriage to the future King Umberto I of Italy. The pre-sale estimate is $2 to $2.4 million.

The centrepiece of Sotheby's sale on Wednesday evening is an emerald and diamond necklace. According to family legend, it is set with emeralds given by Catherine the Great around 1762 to John Hobart, 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire, who served as British ambassador to the Court of St. Petersburg.

His descendant, the 12th Marquis of Lothian, head of an aristocratic Scottish family, is selling the piece, expected to fetch more than $800,000 to finance preservation of historic Ferniehirst Castle in Scotland, one of the family homes.
Sotheby's expects a cushion-shaped 12 carat pink diamond, thought to have belonged to Marie Antoinette, to fetch $400,000.

"It was probably part of the jewels given to her hairdresser Leonard for safekeeping before her flight to Varennes," Bennett told Reuters. "It is the original cutting from the 18th-century and is being sold by a member of a European royal family."
Sotheby's will also offer a collection of Art Nouveau jewllery by Rene Lalique, owned by Japan's Minami Art Museum.
Billed as the single most important group of Lalique jewels to have appeared on the market, the 44 fin-de-siecle lots are expected to bring in some $1.5 million on Wednesday.

Among the Cartier works being sold by Antiquorum Auctioneers and Etude Tajan on Tuesday is a stunning Indian-style platinum necklace set with 29 emeralds worn by film star Merle Oberon. It is expected to fetch $1.5 million.
Cartier pieces which once belonged to Egypt's King Farouk, Morocco's King Hassan, the late pop artist Andy Warhol and Woolworth heiress Barbara Hutton are also on the block.
